newsitem.title: INDIA: Profit-taking, poor demand push Indian sugar down.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking, poor demand push Indian sugar down.

text.p: Indian sugar ended down on reduced demand and selling at higher levels, traders said.
They said fresh seasonal buying petered out at higher levels and light profit-taking by traders also subdued market sentiment.
In ready delivery, sugar S-30 dropped by 5 rupees to 1,495/1,515 rupees per quintal while M-30 fell by two to five rupees to 1,520/1,548 rupees per quintal.
"Supply of sugar from mills to the market however remained light due to limited offerings by millers and higher buying at the mill level in neighbouring states," one trader said.
"Local millers are getting higher enquiries and demand particularly from the southern states like Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh," he said.
Sugar mill delivery remained firm on buying from centres outside Bombay, he said.
In mill delivery, sugar S-30 rose five to 10 rupees to 1,435/1,450 rupees per quintal while sugar M-30 rose 10/20 rupees to 1,460/1,475 rupees per quintal.
